comparator.name: Economics and Business Economics
comparator.sourceNotes: The Economics profile follows a common first year. This example takes all four named Economics courses in the final semester. Students may replace one of the four with an approved profile elective. The third-year minor, study abroad or approved internship combination accounts for 30 EC. The required 10 EC thesis has a 120 EC entry threshold, including the full first year, and requires approval of the study plan.

alternatives.label: Economics, policy & quantitative analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is centred on microeconomics, macroeconomics and public policy, supported by business foundations, finance, mathematics, data science, statistics and econometrics.
alternatives.concept: Study how households, firms and governments make economic choices. Use mathematics, statistics and data to examine markets, public policy and finance, then test economic relationships through econometrics.
progression: Economics, accounting and programming establish foundations. Calculus and statistics precede linear algebra, numerical methods and later econometrics. Microeconomics precedes behavioural economics, and market and banking applications conclude the plan.

alternatives.label: Business economics, finance & enterprise
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines accounting and finance with strategy, marketing, entrepreneurship, organisations, leadership, international business and empirical analysis.
alternatives.concept: Explore how firms develop products, understand customers and make financial and strategic decisions. Study accounting, banking, business law and leadership, and use research to evaluate market opportunities.
progression: Business foundations and product design lead to strategy, leadership and marketing. Early data work prepares students for machine learning, while accounting precedes advanced finance. Later courses apply these skills to international business, customer research and econometrics.
alternatives.distinctness: 8 different courses each way from the closest option, with product development, business law, marketing and leadership.

alternatives.label: International economics, sustainability & development
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines economics, international business and econometrics with climate, sustainability governance, renewable systems, environmental justice and comparative institutions.
alternatives.concept: Study trade, public policy and economic choices in the context of climate change. Combine economics and econometrics with environmental data, sustainability governance, environmental justice and renewable-energy design.
progression: Sustainability and economics establish the basis for work in governance and public policy. Data analysis precedes remote sensing and machine learning. Advanced work combines trade and finance, econometrics, environmental justice and renewable-energy design.
alternatives.distinctness: 9 and 11 different courses each way from the first and second options respectively, with climate, geospatial analysis, environmental justice and renewable energy.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic degree with three formal profiles. Economics is the least specialized and most general continuation of the shared curriculum, centred on economic theory, markets, policy and quantitative methods; the choice was made before considering UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest route covers the general Economics profile and its shared quantitative core. The two remaining formal generator-backed profiles, Business Economics and International Economics and Sustainable Development, both yield coherent and feasible UCR curricula with materially different course sets. Three alternatives are therefore included, which is the maximum.

blocks: Both introduce consumer and firm behaviour, markets and microeconomic reasoning.
Both develop macroeconomic analysis of growth, inflation, unemployment and policy.
Both study choice under uncertainty, strategic interaction and market equilibrium. Groningen gives the formal microeconomic models a dedicated course.
Both examine government intervention, taxation, redistribution and public policy.
Both study how observed choices depart from standard economic models. Groningen also teaches experimental methods.
Both introduce business decisions and their economic context. UCR focuses on developing ventures and business models.
Both develop financial accounting and interpretation of financial statements.
Both study financial institutions, markets and banking risk. UCR also examines monetary policy and asset pricing.
Both analyse trade policy and economic integration. UCR also studies cross-border business strategy and market entry.
Mathematical Methods provides calculus and related quantitative foundations for economics.
Research Methods & Statistics provides statistical and empirical-research foundations.
Both develop practical data analysis and visualisation.
Both develop matrix and linear-algebra methods for quantitative analysis.
Econometrics directly develops estimation, testing, causal analysis and prediction.
Both involve designing a question, collecting or using data and reporting findings. Groningen focuses on empirical economics and introduces regression.
Both develop academic writing, evidence-based argument and communication. UCR applies these across disciplines.
Groningen requires a dedicated empirical economics paper before the final year.
Groningen sets aside a semester for an approved minor, study abroad or an internship with courses.
Groningen requires a 10 EC economics thesis. The optional 15 EC UCR research element sits outside the UCR course schedules.

notes.text: Groningen’s Economics profile includes dedicated work in economic theory, empirical research and a required thesis. The UCR examples combine economics with quantitative methods, business or sustainability, and have different requirements.

audience.programmeDescription: Groningen’s Economics and Business Economics degree begins with a shared first year. This example follows the Economics profile, which studies markets, policy and economic behaviour using theory and data.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR examples emphasise quantitative economics, business and finance, or international economics and sustainability.
